\chapter{María, Ven --- Naming Who You Are Talking To}
\label{ch:maria-ven}
\hlchaptermodality{249}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can address somebody by name.}

I can address somebody by name.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[María, ven]{María, ven — naming who you are talking to}

\label{lesson:ES-C64-maria-ven}



\begin{quote}
\emph{Ven} — come. \emph{¿Cómo estás?} — how are you.

Both are aimed at somebody. Now say \textbf{who}.
\end{quote}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: the comma is the grammar}]
\begin{quote}
\emph{\textbf{María}}\emph{, ven.} \emph{¿Cómo estás,} \emph{\textbf{María}}\emph{?} \emph{\textbf{Profesor}}\emph{, ¿puedo hablar?}
\end{quote}

The name can go at the front or at the end, and either way it is fenced off by a \textbf{comma}. That comma is not decoration — it is the entire grammatical marking. There is nothing else to learn here.
\end{grammarlens}

\begin{culture}
Latin had a whole \textbf{case} for this — a set of endings whose only job was addressing somebody. Spanish replaced all of it with a pause.

That is the shortest possible summary of what became of Latin's endings. Twice now you have watched the same thing: the endings went, and something small and audible took over the work — a preposition for the personal \emph{a}, and here a comma.

And notice the person you address takes \textbf{no} \emph{a}. \emph{Veo a María} has María on the receiving end of the seeing; \emph{María, ven} has her doing the coming. Same name, opposite roles, and the comma is what tells them apart.
\end{culture}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{María, ven}
  \item \emph{Veo a María}, then \emph{María, ven}, and hear the difference
\end{itemize}

\emph{Twice through:}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What did Spanish replace Latin's addressing case with? (A \textbf{comma}.)

And does the addressed person take an \emph{a}? (\textbf{No.})
\end{tcolorbox}
